The '''''Sahih International translation''''' is an [[English translations of the Quran|English-language translation]] of the [[Quran]]. Published by the Publishing House ''Dar [[Abul Qasim]]'' in Saudi Arabia, it is one of the world's most popular Quran translations.<ref name=DB>{{cite web|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/how-three-american-women-translated-one-of-the-worlds-most-popular-qurans|title=How Three American Women Translated One of the World's Most Popular Qurans|first=Katie|last=Zavadski|date=26 March 2017|publisher=|via=www.thedailybeast.com}}</ref>

Translated by three American women, Umm Muhammad (Emily Assami), Mary Kennedy, and Amatullah Bantley,<ref>: 1997, [[The Qur’ān]]  [Saheeh International]] Translation</ref> it uses un-archaic language.<ref name=DAQ>[http://etheses.whiterose.ac.uk/9013/1/Somia%20Refai%20eThesis%20May%202015.pdf Dogmatic Approaches of Qur’ān Translators: Linguistic and Theological Issues], Somia Qudah-Refai</ref> Notable conventions include rendering the [[God in Islam]] as ''[[Allah]]'' as they believe it is not acceptable to use the English word. 

The translation has been described as biased towards "[[Sunni orthodoxy]]," which, according to authors, requires words to be inserted in square parentheses.<ref>"The Quran: A Complete Revelation", 2016, [[Sam Gerrans]].</ref><ref name="DB3">{{cite web|last=Zavadski|first=Katie|date=26 March 2017|title=How Three American Women Translated One of the World's Most Popular Qurans|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/how-three-american-women-translated-one-of-the-worlds-most-popular-qurans|publisher=|via=www.thedailybeast.com}}</ref> It has been sponsored and promoted by [[Salafi movement|Salafi]] followers. For those reasons, it has been defined as an [[International propagation of Salafism and Wahhabism|ultraconservative]] translation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bakhtiar|first=Laleh|date=2011|title=The misinterpretation of Chapter 4 Verse 34|url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1350506811415206|journal=European Journal of Women's Studies|language=en|volume=18|issue=4|pages=431–439|doi=10.1177/1350506811415206|s2cid=144003408|issn=1350-5068|via=|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

''[[Ṣaḥīḥ]]'' ({{lang|ar|{{big|صحيح}}}}) may be translated as "[[wiktionary:sahih|authentic]]"<ref>[https://translate.google.co.uk/?hl=en&tab=wT1#view=home&op=translate&sl=ar&tl=en&text=%D8%B5%D8%AD%D9%8A%D8%AD Google Translate]</ref> or "sound."<ref name="Dickinson-p5">{{cite book |page=5 |author=Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ |translator=Dr. Eerik Dickinson |title=An Introduction to the Science of the Ḥadīth |publisher=Garnet Publishing Limited |location=Reading |year=2006 |isbn=1-85964-158-X |url=http://www.kalamullah.com/Books/Ibn-as-Salaah-s-Introduction-to-the-Science-of-Hadeeth.pdf |accessdate=2019-11-30}}</ref>

==Translators==
Emily Assami was born in [[California]] into an [[atheist]] family.<ref name="The-Daily-Beast-2017">{{Cite web |date=2017-04-10 |title=How Three American Women Translated One of the World’s Most Popular Qurans |url= https://www.thedailybeast.com/how-three-american-women-translated-one-of-the-worlds-most-popular-qurans |access-date=2024-04-06 |website=Daily Beast |language=en}}</ref> She studied Arabic at [[Damascus University]]. She converted to Islam and is known as ''Umm Muhammad'' or ''Aminah''.<ref name="Arab-News-2010">{{Cite web |date=2010-12-11 |title=Saheeh International: One for the books |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/362726 |access-date=2021-03-27 |website=Arab News |language=en}}</ref>

Mary Kennedy was born in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]]. She was a former Christian who converted to Islam.{{r|Arab-News-2010}}

Amatullah Bantley was a former Catholic Christian. She was introduced to Islam through international Muslim students. She converted to Islam in 1986 and eventually moved to Saudi Arabia.{{r|Arab-News-2010}}

extract:
The Sahih International translation is an English-language translation of the Quran. Published by the Publishing House Dar Abul Qasim in Saudi Arabia, it is one of the world's most popular Quran translations.
Translated by three American women, Umm Muhammad (Emily Assami), Mary Kennedy, and Amatullah Bantley, it uses un-archaic language. Notable conventions include rendering the God in Islam as Allah as they believe it is not acceptable to use the English word. 
The translation has been described as biased towards "Sunni orthodoxy," which, according to authors, requires words to be inserted in square parentheses. It has been sponsored and promoted by Salafi followers. For those reasons, it has been defined as an ultraconservative translation.
Ṣaḥīḥ (صحيح) may be translated as "authentic" or "sound."
